_comment: The runner host's layout, read by host/rf-host-apply, supervisor/rf-supervisor, supervisor/rf-jit and host-setup.sh. CPU numbers are this machine's (core i = CPUs i and i+8; see /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/topology/thread_siblings_list). The values measured on this host (the fixed frequency policy "freq" and the cache and memory-bandwidth partition "resctrl") are not in the repository: host-setup.sh merges them from the host-only file /etc/rf-runner/host.local.json (template: host.local.json.example) into the installed /opt/rf-runner/slots.json. Each slot's tap, mac and net must equal the sets vm_src and vm_proxy in host/rf.nft and the http_port lines of host/proxy/squid.conf (host-setup.sh checks). Each slot runs as its own user (`user`: its supervisor, its QEMU, its tap, its run directory; the token broker maps the requesting uid to the slot). The bench VM's memory is backed by reserved 2 MiB hugepages (`hugepages`; rf-host-apply reserves them). Runner labels: a JIT runner gets exactly the labels listed (GitHub adds no self-hosted label), so a bare `runs-on: self-hosted` matches none of them. hard_limit_s bounds one VM's one job, counted from its start: the longest job on bench is the certificate (timeout-minutes 60 with nanoda, else 50; setup and setup-tools 30, benchmark 50), so bench is 60 + 30 minutes of margin for GitHub's cancellation and the job's cleanup = 5400 s; the longest light job is sync (30 minutes), so light is 3600 s. GitHub's own timeout ends a job first; the hard limit only frees a stuck VM.

bandwidth._comment: per tap, tc (rf-host-apply): down = host to VM (tbf), up = VM to host (ingress police)
